user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Aggressive 40% discounting: +31% short-term signups, -12% retention churn. Unsustainable long-term play. Standard SMB segment.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
The two live symptoms (activation -6% QoQ, onboarding completion -4% QoQ) point at the funnel itself, not at price. Promotional pricing is the tempting reflex given the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 records exactly that trade: +31% signups against -12% retention churn, which is a direct loss against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) act on established customers and do not touch the declining activation/onboarding metrics. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment from the one under competitive pressure and would not move the observed declines. That leaves simplify_onboarding and activation_messaging; onboarding is upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly moves both numbers, and it is supported by two independent inherited records (memory_31 on signup field reduction, memory_86 on shortened onboarding).

I am spending both verification pulls on the two memories that are load-bearing for the action I intend rather than on the ones I am rejecting. memory_31 is from day 12 and memory_86 from day 52; both are consolidated summaries whose original records I have not seen. I specifically want to check: whether memory_31's "durable lift" was measured past the first week or only at first-week activation (the summary is ambiguous and a first-week-only measurement would not support a long-term revenue claim), and whether memory_86's adoption lift was gross or net of any quality effect. Rejecting promotional_pricing on memory_73 alone is defensible without a pull because even a generous reading of that record still shows retention damage.

Downstream value risk is real and I am flagging it rather than treating the memories as settling the question. Cutting required signup fields removes qualification data; memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path, and thinner signup data could degrade routing into that path. So the mechanism that lifts SMB activation could quietly reduce qualified revenue mix. The experiment must therefore be instrumented on qualified-revenue and lead-routing quality, not just completion and activation rates, and must run long enough to see retention rather than reading a week-one bump as success.

Standard experiment scale: the symptom is current and measured, and two inherited records converge, which is enough to justify more than a token test. But the underlying evidence is inherited summary rather than anything I have observed, the competitive environment on day 76 differs from day 12, and the downstream mix risk argues against a broad rollout. If verification shows memory_31's lift was only ever measured at week one, I would drop to a small guarded test or switch to activation_messaging (memory_91), which is reversible and carries no data-quality cost.
